analysis:
Examined both SSDBlockIndex revisions, its patch, cache-reference excerpts and coordinator metadata/bounded patch context against the definition index and detailed T-041. SSDBlockIndex.swift:137-140 adds a locked recency accessor; :229-231 and :288-295 propagate an optional TTL cutoff to owned retirement. Existing default nil preserves non-TTL retirement semantics. No visible change exposes payloads or raw prefix hashes, changes account scope, raises TTL, alters encryption/key handling, or changes authorization/billing. docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md:377 and :381 describe preserving recently hit entries despite lagging file mtimes and bounded retirement slices; these are consistent with the existing sliding-TTL contract, not evidence of a longer reuse window. Diagnostics at :546-551 describe existing metadata/counters, not a demonstrated new disclosure.
Remaining integration checks are material to T-041/A-001 and availability: verify SSDOwnedEntryRetirement consumes unusedSince under an exclusive lease and epoch ownership check, preserves only genuinely recent hits, and persists recency safely; verify SSDWholeRootMaintainer supplies the cutoff only for TTL retirement, not budget eviction. The partial SSDCheckpointFileCoordinator.swift patch introduces shared/exclusive modes and nonwaiting upgrade, but its acquisition, cancellation, release and queue implementation is not supplied here. Integration must verify fairness, cancellation cleanup, mutation exclusion and lock ordering with SSDDiskBudget's lock (SSDBlockIndex.swift:290-295), plus read/authentication failure and maintenance callers. No concrete regression is established in this local scope; documentation assertions do not verify these cross-file controls.
